question.text: Meenakshi Capital is evaluating whether to engage a Placement Agent (PA) for its maiden INR 500 crore Cat II fundraise. From the Manager's perspective, the Placement Agent's PRIMARY role is:

answer.text: Distribution of fund units through a private-placement fundraise, widening investor reach (HNIs, family offices, institutional LPs) and typically earning a placement fee based on capital raised.
Acting as the SEBI-registered Trustee for the Trust-structured AIF.
Performing the annual statutory audit of the AIF.
Issuing the custodian certificate for commodity derivative physical settlement.

explanation.text: The Logic: A Placement Agent (a category of distributor) facilitates private-placement fundraising — connecting the Manager with qualified investors, managing investor pitch-books, and handling subscription logistics. Fees are typically a percentage of capital raised (commonly 1-3% of commitments from investors they source), or a retainer plus success fee. The Trap: Options B, C, D swap roles with trustee, auditor and custodian respectively. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) is tuned for the DISTRIBUTOR's view of this role; XIX-C asks managers how to CHOOSE and MONITOR placement agents. XV/X-A do not cover placement agency. Manager's Pro-Tip: Benchmark the placement fee to the investor tier. A 2.5% fee for a USD 50 million sovereign wealth cheque is extractive; 1% or flat retainer is fairer. Always negotiate a 'cap per investor' clause.
